title: Evaluating large language models in medical applications: a survey

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM sensitivity to answer positions in bilingual multiple-choice questions (MCQs), specifically tracking the tendency to systematically choose answers located in the first position.

Comparing model accuracy across different specialized medical examination subjects (e.g., observing high accuracy in medical humanities versus lower accuracy in pathology) to detect skewed knowledge representation.

Conducting cross-lingual evaluations (e.g., using both English and Spanish prompts) on medical image classification datasets to identify and reduce performance disparities and community bias when processing non-English data.

Using human assessment, Likert scales, and comprehensive evaluation frameworks (such as the 12-aspect framework by Singhal et al.) to manually rate the possibility of bias, inaccuracies, and missing content in medical summaries and open-ended clinical question answering.
